import numpy as np


def bistatic_doppler(p, v, tx, rx, lam):
    """Doppler shift (Hz) of the echo off an aircraft at p (m) moving at v (m/s), transmitter tx, receiver rx."""
    p, v, tx, rx = (np.asarray(a, float) for a in (p, v, tx, rx))
    u_rx = (p - rx) / np.linalg.norm(p - rx)      # unit vector receiver -> aircraft
    u_tx = (p - tx) / np.linalg.norm(p - tx)      # unit vector transmitter -> aircraft
    return -(np.dot(v, u_rx) - np.dot(v, u_tx)) / lam

import numpy as np
import pytest

from subject_under_test import bistatic_doppler


def test_bistatic_doppler_basic_scalar_case():
    p = (10.0, 0.0)
    v = (1.0, 0.0)
    tx = (0.0, 0.0)
    rx = (0.0, 10.0)
    lam = 1.0

    expected = 1.0 - 1.0 / np.sqrt(2.0)
    assert bistatic_doppler(p, v, tx, rx, lam) == pytest.approx(expected)


def test_bistatic_doppler_zero_when_velocity_is_perpendicular_to_both_lines_of_sight():
    p = (1.0, 1.0)
    v = (0.0, 1.0)
    tx = (0.0, 0.0)
    rx = (2.0, 0.0)
    lam = 3.0

    assert bistatic_doppler(p, v, tx, rx, lam) == pytest.approx(0.0)


def test_bistatic_doppler_changes_sign_with_velocity_reversal():
    p = (10.0, 0.0)
    v = (1.0, 0.0)
    tx = (0.0, 0.0)
    rx = (0.0, 10.0)
    lam = 1.0

    forward = bistatic_doppler(p, v, tx, rx, lam)
    reverse = bistatic_doppler(p, (-v[0], -v[1]), tx, rx, lam)

    assert reverse == pytest.approx(-forward)


def test_bistatic_doppler_simple_integer_result():
    p = (1.0, 0.0)
    v = (1.0, 0.0)
    tx = (0.0, 0.0)
    rx = (2.0, 0.0)
    lam = 2.0

    assert bistatic_doppler(p, v, tx, rx, lam) == pytest.approx(1.0)


def test_bistatic_doppler_3d_case():
    p = (0.0, 0.0, 1.0)
    v = (0.0, 0.0, 2.0)
    tx = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    rx = (0.0, 1.0, 0.0)
    lam = 4.0

    expected = (2.0 - np.sqrt(2.0)) / 4.0
    assert bistatic_doppler(p, v, tx, rx, lam) == pytest.approx(expected)


def test_bistatic_doppler_accepts_list_inputs_and_returns_expected_value():
    p = [3.0, 4.0]
    v = [2.0, -1.0]
    tx = [0.0, 0.0]
    rx = [6.0, 8.0]
    lam = 5.0

    # u_tx = (3, 4)/5, u_rx = (-3, -4)/5
    # dot(v, u_tx) = 2*(3/5) + (-1)*(4/5) = 2/5
    # dot(v, u_rx) = -2/5
    # return = -((-2/5) - (2/5)) / 5 = 4/25
    assert bistatic_doppler(p, v, tx, rx, lam) == pytest.approx(4.0 / 25.0)
